messages:
elaine: Quick report: reproducible flakiness in js/python SDKs when streaming responses plus aggressive load-balancer timeouts. If LB sends FIN mid-event we sometimes lose the trailing bytes and then a reconnect duplicates the tail.

ryan: Can you paste a tiny capture of the recv boundaries?

elaine: Sure, simplified raw chunks we saw:

```
data: {"text":"Hel"}

# LB FIN here, no extra LF
<FIN>

data: {"text":"lo"}

```

Client behavior: when FIN arrives without the trailing separator some SDK readers treat the buffer as incomplete and discard, then on reconnect the server resends the last part and client emits 'lo' twice.

pat: We've fixed similar issues by treating EOF as an implicit event separator and by using incremental UTF-8 decoders so multibyte chars aren't mangled. Also ensure reconnect swaps are serialized (pause consumer -> drain leftover -> swap -> resume).

ryan: Agree. Another tweak: if an event contains only whitespace or empty data after trimming, skip emitting it; that filters stray empty tokens from comment-only lines. But keep logging in sse-debug mode.

elaine: I opened PR #9999 with a tiny change for python/js: on socket close, append '\\n\\n' to leftover buffer before processing; add tests simulating FIN between bytes and a bounded incremental decoder. Test passes locally.

ci-bot: PR #9999 opened by elaine - summary: sdk: treat EOF as SSE boundary, use incremental decoding, serialize reconnect swap, add split-chunk tests

pat: Can you also add a small quickstart note about LB idle timeouts and recommending keepalive comments rather than closing mid-event? That helps integrators.

elaine: Added a short note in dev_docs/streaming.md and a sample script to fuzz chunk boundaries. CI green. Planning to merge after one more review.

ryan: Thanks — this should reduce duplicate tails and broken multibyte tokens in the field.
